title: NJ Driver's Manual – Chapter 1
subtitle: Driver Licensing & Requirements
note: Based on the 2025 NJ Driver's Manual, Chapter 1. Verify all answers against the current manual before your exam.

questions.q: What is the minimum age to apply for a New Jersey examination permit (learner's permit)?
questions.exp: In New Jersey, applicants must be at least 16 years old to apply for an examination permit.

questions.q: Under NJ's Graduated Driver License (GDL) program, what is the minimum time a driver who receives their permit before age 17 must hold it before applying for a probationary license?
questions.exp: Drivers who obtain their permit before turning 17 must hold it until age 17 — a minimum of 1 year.

questions.q: How many total hours of supervised driving must a GDL permit holder complete before taking the road skills test?
questions.exp: GDL permit holders must log at least 50 hours of supervised driving practice before applying for a probationary license.

questions.q: Of the required supervised driving hours, how many must be completed during nighttime hours?
questions.exp: At least 10 of the 50 required supervised hours must be driven after dark.

questions.q: During what hours are GDL probationary license holders prohibited from driving unsupervised?
questions.exp: GDL probationary drivers may not drive between 11:01 PM and 5:00 AM unless a licensed driver aged 21+ is in the front seat or it is a documented emergency.

questions.q: During the FIRST YEAR of holding a GDL probationary license, how many non-immediate-family passengers under age 21 may the driver carry?
questions.exp: For the first year of the probationary period, the driver may carry no more than 1 passenger under 21 who is not an immediate family member.

questions.q: Which statement about cell phone use is TRUE for GDL permit and probationary license holders in NJ?
opts: Only texting while driving is prohibited
All cell phone use — handheld AND hands-free — is prohibited
Cell phones may be used when stopped at a red light
questions.exp: GDL permit and probationary holders are prohibited from using any wireless communication device while driving, including hands-free devices.

questions.q: What is the minimum age of the licensed driver who must supervise a GDL examination permit holder?
questions.exp: The supervising licensed driver must be at least 21 years old and seated in the front passenger seat.

questions.q: Under what condition may a GDL probationary driver legally drive during the nighttime curfew hours?
opts: A parent has provided written permission
The driver has held the probationary license for over 6 months
A licensed driver aged 21 or older is in the front seat, or it is a documented emergency
The driver is traveling directly to or from work
questions.exp: The curfew restriction is lifted when a licensed driver 21 or older is seated in the front seat, or when a documented emergency exists.

questions.q: What license class is required to operate a standard non-commercial passenger vehicle in New Jersey?
questions.exp: Class D is the standard passenger vehicle license in New Jersey, used for everyday driving of cars and light trucks.

questions.q: Which CDL class authorizes the operation of combination vehicles with a GCWR of 26,001 lbs or more when the towed unit exceeds 10,000 lbs?
questions.exp: A Class A CDL is required for combination vehicles where the GCWR is 26,001 lbs or more and the towed unit exceeds 10,000 lbs.

questions.q: Which CDL class covers heavy straight vehicles with a GVWR of 26,001 lbs or more (not towing over 10,000 lbs)?
questions.exp: A Class B CDL authorizes operation of heavy straight vehicles with a GVWR of 26,001 lbs or more, plus towing a unit not exceeding 10,000 lbs.

questions.q: A REAL ID-compliant New Jersey driver's license or ID card is identified by which marking?
opts: A blue star in the upper right
A gold star in the upper right
questions.exp: A gold star in the upper right corner of an NJ license or ID indicates it meets federal REAL ID Act standards.

questions.q: For which activities is a REAL ID-compliant license (or another acceptable federal document) now required?
opts: Registering a vehicle or renewing insurance
Boarding domestic commercial flights and entering certain federal facilities
Applying for a New Jersey driver's license
questions.exp: As of May 7, 2025, a REAL ID-compliant document is required to board domestic commercial flights and access certain federal facilities.

questions.q: What is the minimum visual acuity (in the better eye, with correction if used) required for a standard NJ driver's license?
questions.exp: Applicants must achieve at least 20/40 vision in the better eye — with or without corrective lenses — to qualify for a standard license.

questions.q: If a driver requires corrective lenses to meet the 20/40 vision standard, what restriction appears on their NJ license?
opts: Must wear corrective lenses while driving
questions.exp: A 'corrective lenses required' restriction is printed on the license of any driver who needs glasses or contacts to meet the minimum vision standard.

questions.q: Which statement about color blindness and obtaining a NJ driver's license is CORRECT?
opts: Color blindness automatically disqualifies an applicant
Color blind drivers are restricted to daytime driving only
Color blindness alone does not disqualify a person from obtaining a license
Color blind applicants must pass a special color-perception road test
questions.exp: Color blindness alone does not disqualify an applicant. The key vision requirement is acuity (sharpness), not color perception.

questions.q: How long is a standard New Jersey driver's license valid before renewal is required?
questions.exp: A standard NJ driver's license is valid for 4 years from the date of issuance.

questions.q: How long is a New Jersey examination permit (learner's permit) valid once issued?
questions.exp: A NJ examination permit is valid for 2 years from the date it is issued.

questions.q: What is the minimum age at which a GDL driver may obtain a probationary license?
questions.exp: Drivers who obtained their permit before age 17 must wait until they turn 17 before they can apply for a probationary license.

questions.q: What is the name of the New Jersey agency responsible for issuing driver's licenses?
questions.exp: New Jersey uses the Motor Vehicle Commission (MVC) — not a DMV — to issue driver's licenses, IDs, and vehicle registrations.

questions.q: How many points of identification must an applicant earn under NJ's Six-Point ID Verification System?
questions.exp: Applicants must accumulate at least 6 points of identification from approved documents to verify identity and lawful presence.

questions.q: Which of the following is TRUE about NJ's Six-Point ID Verification System?
opts: The same document may be used twice to earn double points
Only documents issued in the U.S. are accepted
No single document may be counted more than once
A Social Security card alone satisfies the full 6 points
questions.exp: Each document can only be counted once — the same document cannot be used to satisfy multiple point categories.

questions.q: In NJ's Six-Point ID system, how many points is a valid U.S. Passport worth?
questions.exp: A valid U.S. Passport earns 4 points as primary proof of identity in NJ's Six-Point ID Verification System.

questions.q: In NJ's Six-Point ID system, how many points is a U.S. Birth Certificate worth?
questions.exp: A U.S. Birth Certificate is worth 4 points, serving as primary proof of identity.

questions.q: In NJ's Six-Point ID Verification System, which of the following is typically worth 2 points (secondary proof)?
questions.exp: A NJ Vehicle Registration is a secondary document worth 2 points in the six-point system.

questions.q: What does the organ donor designation on a NJ driver's license indicate?
opts: The holder receives priority on transplant waiting lists
Medical personnel may access health records in an emergency
The holder has decided to donate organs, tissues, and eyes upon death
The license fee was reduced through a donation program
questions.exp: The organ donor designation signals the holder's decision to donate organs, tissues, and eyes in the event of their death.

questions.q: Where must the supervising licensed driver be seated when a GDL examination permit holder is operating a vehicle?
opts: Anywhere in the vehicle with a clear view
In the back seat directly behind the driver
Either front seat position is acceptable
questions.exp: The supervising licensed driver (21 or older) must be seated in the front passenger seat at all times.

questions.q: What is the key difference between a NJ examination permit and a probationary license?
opts: A permit is valid only in NJ; a probationary license is valid in all 50 states
A permit requires a licensed driver in the front seat at all times; a probationary license allows solo driving (with GDL restrictions)
A probationary license allows highway driving; a permit does not
A permit is free; a probationary license requires a fee
questions.exp: The major distinction is that a probationary license allows the holder to drive solo — without a supervising driver — though GDL curfew and passenger restrictions still apply.

questions.q: To which age group does New Jersey's Graduated Driver License (GDL) program apply?
opts: All new drivers, regardless of age
questions.exp: The GDL program applies to drivers under 18. Those who first obtain a license at age 18 or older follow a non-GDL path.

questions.q: If a GDL probationary license holder is convicted of a moving violation, what happens to their probationary period?
opts: They must retake the written knowledge test
They must complete a court-ordered driving course
questions.exp: A moving violation conviction during the GDL probationary period results in an extension of that probationary period.

questions.q: What must a GDL permit holder complete BEFORE taking the NJ road skills test?
opts: Hold the permit for the required period AND complete 50 supervised driving hours (including 10 at night)
Complete a mandatory classroom driver-education course
Obtain a letter of approval from a licensed driving instructor
questions.exp: Before taking the road skills test, an applicant must hold the permit for the required period and log at least 50 supervised hours (10 at night).

questions.q: For a first-time NJ license applicant, which test is required to obtain an examination permit?
opts: Both a written test and a road skills test
questions.exp: Only the written knowledge test is required to obtain an examination permit. The road skills test comes later, for the probationary license.

questions.q: How many questions appear on the standard NJ written knowledge test for a Class D license?
questions.exp: The standard NJ knowledge test for a Class D license contains 40 multiple-choice questions.

questions.q: What is the minimum passing score (percentage) on the NJ driver's written knowledge test?
questions.exp: Applicants must answer at least 80% of questions correctly (32 out of 40) to pass the NJ knowledge test.

questions.q: If an applicant fails the NJ knowledge test, how long must they wait before retaking it?
questions.exp: Applicants who fail the NJ written knowledge test must wait at least 2 weeks before retaking the test.

questions.q: Is obtaining a REAL ID-compliant NJ driver's license mandatory for all NJ residents?
opts: Yes, all residents must upgrade by the federal deadline
No — it is voluntary; residents may choose a standard (non-REAL ID) license
Only required for residents who fly domestically more than twice per year
Only required for residents born outside the United States
questions.exp: A REAL ID-compliant license is voluntary. Residents may choose a standard license, though it cannot be used for domestic air travel or to enter certain federal facilities.

questions.q: In New Jersey, within how many days must a driver notify the MVC after changing their address?
questions.exp: New Jersey law requires drivers to notify the MVC within 1 week (7 days) of a change of address.

questions.q: Which additional license or endorsement is required to operate a motorcycle in New Jersey?
opts: A motorcycle (MC) license or a motorcycle endorsement on a Class D license
No additional endorsement — any license permits motorcycle operation
questions.exp: To operate a motorcycle in NJ you must hold either a standalone motorcycle license or an MC endorsement added to your Class D license.

questions.q: A Class C CDL in New Jersey is required for which type of vehicle?
opts: Vehicles designed to carry 16 or more persons (including driver), or those placarded for hazardous materials
Tow trucks and recovery vehicles only
questions.exp: A Class C CDL is required for vehicles designed to transport 16 or more persons (including the driver), or vehicles carrying placarded quantities of hazardous materials.

questions.q: Which of the following statements about a New Jersey examination permit is TRUE?
opts: It allows solo driving between sunrise and sunset
It permits driving only on local streets, not highways
A licensed driver 21 or older must be in the front passenger seat whenever the permit holder drives
It is valid for 5 years from the date of issue
questions.exp: Whenever a GDL examination permit holder is behind the wheel, a licensed driver who is at least 21 years old must be seated in the front passenger seat.
